chapter: Ellington band members and life on the road
title: Hodges, the girl in Washington, and the gun in her purse
summary: Hodges got Bigard to throw out a tough girlfriend at a Washington boarding house until Bigard found a gun in her purse.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, because I used to -- he and I used to be buddy-buddy on the road, you know. And the only time I -- he used to fool around quite a bit. And so we were in Washington, D.C., and they had a gal there, she was after Johnny and Johnny was after her, too. And then we got together and Johnny and I, we had -- in the lady's house she had a double room, like, you know, like, because you can close these doors here?

Well, there would be one for him and one for me, while we stayed there. We had been staying there every time we went to Washington. So Johnny, he got tired of this girl, and this gal was a roughy, a real toughie, too. So he'd depend on me, when he got tired, for me to put them out, you know. So she had her bag on the dresser like, so Johnny said, "Man, get rid of her for me." I said, "Why don't you get rid of her yourself?" He said, "Well, no, man, she's too much for me. You get rid of her, man."

So I'm grabbing this girl by the arm and said, "C'mon, you got to go." She said, "I'm not going nowhere," and she was using all kind of vile language, you know. And I said, "Oh, we can't stand -- we can't have this in the house." And her purse was on this dresser. So I said, "Oh, yeah," and I'm pulling on her. You know, I'm starting to get rough with her? And I said, "Here. Take your purse and get on out of
here." And I picked up the purse and I feel a gun in there. You ought to see the big change.

"How long you want to stay in here?" I said, "Johnny shouldn't act that way with you. Where's that character?" I said, "Go get him." So Johnny said, "Put her out." I said, "You put her out. She's got a gun in that bag." He changed, too. I said, "No, you do your own work now, Bub." He was something else.
